 Community and lifestyle
 15 questions 
 What SeaFlower is, how it is laid out, and what daily life looks like.
 What is SeaFlower and where exactly is it? SeaFlower is a 1,175-acre master-planned coastal village in west Bradenton, Florida (ZIP 34210), in unincorporated Manatee County, bordered by Cortez Road West on the north, 75th Street West on the east and 86th Street West on the west. It sits on the former Preston family flower farm. Phase One is 400 acres around the 19-acre Lake Flores with 1,063 homes, apartments, a hotel and a Publix-anchored Village Center; full buildout is about 4,000 homes. The Welcome Center is at 4505 Flower Fields Trail, (941) 212-0801.

 Who is the developer? Lake Flores Land Company, led by principal Ed Hill, with LAMB Properties as investment partner. The brand and site plan are held by Cortez75W Investors, LLC. The plan was approved by Manatee County in 2015 under the name Lake Flores and rebranded SeaFlower before launch in 2024.

 Is SeaFlower a 55+ or age-restricted community? No. SeaFlower is an all-ages community. Every builder lists it as non-age-restricted and the developer markets it for every stage of life.

 Is SeaFlower gated? No gates appear on the site plan or in any developer material, and the internal streets are being turned over to Manatee County as public roads. Treat it as a non-gated community.

 What amenities are there, and when do they open? The Garden Club is the resident-only amenity campus on Lake Flores Park: Plumeria Hall (lounge, catering kitchen, conference room), a Gathering Hall for events, a fitness center with studio, a zero-entry resort pool with lap lanes and spa, four pickleball courts, an event lawn and amphitheater, a fire pit and a playground. It broke ground in July 2025 and is scheduled to open in fall 2026. Around it are the 2.5-mile Lake Flores Trail, a nature trail, two dog parks and pocket parks.

 Is there really only one pool for 4,000 homes? For Phase One, yes: one amenity campus, The Garden Club, serves the 1,063 Phase One homes. Amenity plans for later phases have not been published. In my experience the developer sizes the first amenity center for the first phase and adds facilities as later phases open, but I would not buy on the assumption of a second pool until it is on a plan. The Village Center, the trail and the beach three miles away do a lot of the lifestyle work here.
 Insider perspective 
 Are golf carts allowed? Can I drive one to the beach? The community is designed around a 2.5-mile multi-modal trail built for walking, biking and golf carts, and the developer calls it golf-cart friendly. Driving on public streets is governed by Florida law (Statute 316.212), which allows carts only on roads a county has designated; a street-legal low-speed vehicle with lights, signals and insurance is the safe answer for anything beyond the trail, and Cortez Road to the island is a real road with real traffic. A David Weekley buyer commented that street-legal carts are in use with the right insurance. Confirm the HOA rules before you buy a cart.

 Is it walkable? Is it a real TND? The developer says SeaFlower is inspired by traditional neighborhood design but is not a strict TND. In practice: narrow streets, front porches near the sidewalk, rear-alley garages on many lots, pocket parks, and a mixed-use Village Center reachable by foot or golf cart. Sidewalks and the trail connect the neighborhoods to the amenity center and retail.

 What will the Village Center have, and when does Publix open? About 140,000 square feet of retail, dining and office in phase one, plus roughly 332 to 362 apartments and a 120-room hotel, developed by CASTO and Redstone with apartments by NDC. The anchor is a Publix of about 50,000 square feet with a separate Publix Liquors, slated for fall 2026. Announced tenants include Dutch Bros, Whataburger, Playa Bowls, Potbelly, Dave's Hot Chicken, Pecan Jacks, Nothing Bundt Cakes, Club Pilates, PacDental, PNC Bank and Suncoast Credit Union. Completion is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, with openings staggered.

 Are there apartments or a hotel I can stay in? Both are planned in the Village Center: about 332 to 362 apartments in phase one (600 at buildout) and a 120-room hotel (250 at buildout). No leasing dates, rents or hotel brand have been published as of September 2026.

 How many people live there now, and how fast is it selling? First residents moved in September 2025. The developer reported 200-plus homes sold and 90-plus residents in March 2026; Bradenton Magazine reported 238 sold and 150-plus residents by March 30 and more than 270 sold by June 1, 2026. RCLCO counted 198 new-home contracts in the first half of 2026, which tied SeaFlower for 51st best-selling master-planned community in the country.

 When will SeaFlower be finished? What about Phase Two? Phase One is in construction now: 400 lots were complete and 384 more were under development through 2026, with 784 of 1,063 homesites released by April 2026. Phase Two is expected to start around 2027 depending on market conditions, and the plan is three phases of roughly 400 acres each. A community this size takes a decade or more to finish; buy for what exists and what is funded, not the rendering.

 What are the rules on pets, parking and exterior changes? The HOA's covenants and its Architectural and Landscape Design Guidelines are in the ICON Management portal, behind a resident login, so they are not published here. Two dog parks are planned. A third-party listing site mentions breed restrictions and a limit on the number of pets, which I have not seen in an official document. Ask the builder for the full HOA disclosure package before you sign; Florida law gives you three days to cancel if it is missing.

 Is there a social calendar? Yes. An Art of Living Director employed through the HOA programs events, classes and clubs from Plumeria Hall once The Garden Club opens, and the developer's community relations team runs events in the meantime.

 What do current residents say? There are no independent resident reviews online yet, only the developer's published buyer stories (a downsizing couple from Anna Maria Island, longtime West Bradenton residents, a first-time buyer couple in an M/I villa, and buyers using a Cardel ADU as a separate suite). What I hear on site is consistent: people love the porches and the trail, and the two live complaints are construction traffic and waiting for The Garden Club. Both are temporary.
 Insider perspective 

 Builders and homes
 14 questions 
 Who builds what, what it costs, and what is included.
 Which builders are in SeaFlower and what does each build? Five builders. M/I Homes builds the townhomes (Row Homes) and twin villas (Village Homes). Pulte builds single-family homes in its Scenic, Veranda, Front Porch and Distinctive series on 42-foot to 50-foot lots. David Weekley builds Bungalow homes on 45-foot rear-load lots and Classic homes on 60-foot lots. Cardel builds Cottage (50-foot) and Classic (60-foot) homes with front- or rear-garage versions and garage suites. Issa Homes builds estate homes on 80-foot lakefront lots. Full comparison on the builders page .

 What are the starting prices by builder? As published on September 3, 2026: M/I Homes priced from $399,999; Pulte from $404,990; David Weekley Bungalow homes from the $500s (base plans from $469,990) and Classic homes from the $600s (from $624,990); Cardel from the $500s (base plans from $579,990); Issa estate homes from $1,250,000 excluding the homesite premium. All exclude lot premiums, options and closing costs. Every plan is on the homes and pricing page .

 Is the advertised price out the door, or plus the lot? Plus the lot, and plus a lot else. A builder's base price is the plan on a standard lot with standard finishes and the base elevation. Add the homesite premium (quoted separately), structural options, design-center selections, sometimes a premium elevation, and closing costs. Quick move-in homes are the exception: their options are already built in, so the listed price is close to the real number.
 Insider perspective 
 What do quick move-in homes cost and when are they ready? On September 3, 2026 the builders listed about three dozen quick move-in homes, from M/I townhomes at $399,999 to Issa lakefront estates above $1.5 million, with completion dates from ready-now through early 2027. David Weekley's ranged from $574,990 to $882,990; Pulte's from $568,895 to $756,090; Cardel's two Coral plans were in the low $700,000s. The current list is on the homes page , and I keep a weekly version with incentives.

 What is an ADU or garage apartment, and can I have one? An accessory dwelling unit is a separate living space on your lot, either an apartment over the garage or a detached casita connected by a breezeway. SeaFlower received county zoning in 2015 allowing an ADU on every single-family homesite, which is unusual. Cardel offers garage suites on many plans, Pulte's Front Porch series has an ADU version of the Mabel II, Issa offers garage-apartment versions of two plans, and Cardel built the Welcome Center with an 800-square-foot ADU. To rent one you must occupy the main house for a year first, and leases must be at least six months.

 What lot sizes exist, and are there lot premiums? Lots are 42, 45, 50, 60 and 80 feet wide, plus the M/I attached products. Lot premiums are quoted on top of base price for lake, park, corner, oversized and quieter-street lots; Issa's lakefront premiums are quoted only on request. Premiums have been rising as the best lots go; they are also one of the more negotiable numbers on a slow-moving lot.
 Insider perspective 
 Front-load or rear-load garage: what is the difference? Rear-load (alley) garages put the garage door behind the house, so the street side is porch and windows; your driveway is off the alley, which is short. Front-load garages face the street and usually come with a deeper back yard. David Weekley's Bungalow lots are rear-load; Cardel offers both on 50- and 60-foot lots; Pulte offers both. If you want a pool, a boat trailer or a long truck, check the yard depth and alley turning radius before you pick.

 Can I add a private pool? Is there natural gas? Yes to pools on many single-family lots; Cardel advertises the option and Pulte lists quick move-ins with pools. SeaFlower has natural gas service through TECO Peoples Gas; Cardel markets itself as a natural-gas community and David Weekley lists TECO as the gas utility. Which appliances are gas varies by builder and plan.

 What is included versus upgraded, and what does the design center cost? Base specification varies by builder, so ask for the included-features sheet in writing. Cardel's own FAQ says buyers typically spend 10% to 20% of base price in the design center; in my experience 5% to 15% is typical across production builders, with structural options on top. Structural choices (extra garage, extended lanai, bonus room, ADU) must be made before the slab. Cardel was offering up to $20,000 toward design options in September 2026.
 Insider perspective 
 How long does it take to build? Cardel quotes 9 to 14 months from a fully signed contract. Production builders like Pulte, David Weekley and M/I are usually faster once the lot is released, often 7 to 10 months, but lot-release timing adds to that. Quick move-in homes listed in September 2026 were completing between October 2026 and January 2027. Get the schedule in writing with the milestones that trigger your deposits.
 Insider perspective 
 What warranties do the builders give? David Weekley: a 1-2-10 multi-level warranty (one year workmanship, two years mechanical systems, ten years structural) with a personal warranty representative. Pulte: a 10-year limited structural warranty that transfers to later owners. Issa: one year materials and workmanship, two years roofing, plumbing, electrical and HVAC, ten years structural through RWC. M/I publishes a 10-year transferable structural warranty and one-year customer care coverage. Cardel's terms are not on its public pages. Read the actual warranty document, not the brochure.

 Are the homes hurricane-rated? Do they have impact windows? All are built to the current Florida Building Code, which is updated every three years and cannot be weakened locally on wind resistance. Developer materials describe impact glass or shutters, reinforced block first floors and underground utilities across the community, and Pulte lists specific quick move-ins with impact glass. Which builders include impact glass as standard versus shutters varies by plan and elevation; I confirm it plan by plan.

 Should I get my own inspection on a brand-new home? Yes, every time. A builder's own quality walk is not an independent inspection. I bring a third-party inspector at pre-drywall (when framing, plumbing and electrical are visible), at final walkthrough with blue tape, and again before the one-year warranty expires. I did the final quality walk for David Weekley for a living; I still hire an inspector for my clients.
 Insider perspective 
 Can I make changes after I sign? Structural changes generally cannot be made after contract; Cardel's FAQ says so explicitly and the production builders work the same way because materials are ordered early. Design selections have a cutoff date too, usually a few weeks after contract. Builders also do not accept owner-supplied flooring, counters or cabinets.

 Prices, HOA, CDD, taxes and insurance
 11 questions 
 The recurring numbers and the one-time ones.
 What are the HOA fees and what do they cover? $300.88 a month for a single-family home, $308.43 for a townhome and $327.70 for a twin villa, per the developer's December 2025 information sheet and David Weekley's pages. The fee includes 1-Gig fiber internet, front and rear yard landscape maintenance, the parks and trails, and operation of The Garden Club. Townhome and villa fees add exterior maintenance, insurance and reserves. The clubhouse portion is abated until The Garden Club is substantially complete, so expect a step up after it opens.

 Is there a CDD? How much, and for how long? Yes, the Lake Flores Community Development District, created by Manatee County in January 2022. In the FY2027 proposed budget the annual assessment is $1,473 for a townhome, $1,581 for a twin villa, $1,750 to $2,979 for Phase 1B1 lots, $2,092 to $3,409 for Phase 1B2 lots, and $3,335 to $4,605 for Phase 1C lots, depending on lot width. Debt portions run until the bonds mature (2054 to 2056) and can be prepaid; the operations portion (about $400) continues. Full tables on the costs page .

 Why do two homes on the same size lot have different CDD fees? Because they are in different phases with different bond series. Phase 1B lots are on the 2023 bonds, and much of one series was prepaid by builders at lot closing, which lowered those assessments in FY2027. Phase 1C lots are on the $20.9 million Series 2026 bonds issued in February 2026, which is why a 50-foot lot there is about $3,899 a year versus $2,280 in Phase 1B2. Ask which phase your lot is in before you compare.

 Do I pay HOA and CDD before the amenities are built? Yes. HOA dues start at closing; the CDD assessment appears on the tax bill once the lot is on the roll. The developer has abated the clubhouse portion of the HOA until The Garden Club opens, which is the one concession. Every master-planned community works this way in its first years; the trail, parks and lawn service you are paying for exist now, the pool does not yet.

 What will my property taxes be? The tax district covering SeaFlower (Cedar Hammock Fire Control District, unincorporated Manatee County) adopted 14.6100 mills for 2025; David Weekley's pages show 14.671, the 2024 rate. Rule of thumb: taxable value times 1.46%, plus the CDD assessment. A $600,000 home with a $50,000 homestead exemption is roughly $8,000 a year before the CDD. Use the Manatee County Property Appraiser's estimator for a specific parcel.

 Why is the first year's tax bill so low on a new home? Florida assesses property as of January 1. If the house was not substantially complete on January 1, the first bill is based on the land only, which is why listing sites show current taxes of $500 to $1,300 on new SeaFlower homes. The following year it jumps to the full value. Your lender's escrow should assume the full number from day one; check that it does.

 How does the homestead exemption work on a new build? Own and occupy the home as your permanent residence on January 1, then file by March 1 (Manatee County accepts applications online). It removes up to $50,000 of assessed value and caps future assessment increases at 3% a year. You will need a Florida driver license or ID, Florida vehicle registration and voter registration or a declaration of domicile. If you sell a Florida homestead to move here, portability can bring part of your old cap with you.

 What closing costs should I expect? Budget 2% to 3% of price before builder credits: lender fees, title, recording, prepaid taxes and insurance, and documentary stamps on the deed at $0.70 per $100 of price. Who pays doc stamps and title is contractual; builders usually shift them to the buyer while offering a closing-cost credit through their affiliated lender. I show clients the net number both ways.
 Insider perspective 
 How much is homeowners insurance on a new home here? No public quotes exist, and I will not invent one. New homes built to the current code with impact openings earn the wind-mitigation credits Florida requires insurers to give, so premiums are meaningfully lower than for older homes near the coast. Recent client quotes for new single-family homes in this area have run roughly $2,500 to $7,000 a year depending on coverage, elevation and features. Get a quote before contract and write an insurance contingency into the offer.
 Insider perspective 
 How much is the deposit, and is it refundable? It varies by builder. Cardel takes a $5,000 lot deposit plus a pre-approval to reserve, with more due at contract and design. Production builders typically take a percentage of base price at contract plus deposits on options. Florida requires deposits up to 10% of price to be escrowed unless you waive it in writing. Refundability depends entirely on the contract's default clause, which is the paragraph to read twice.

 Are there special assessments or transfer fees? The HOA disclosure summary Florida requires must warn that assessments may change and unpaid ones can become a lien. A capital contribution or working-capital fee at closing is common in new communities but is not published for SeaFlower; ask for it in writing. If you did not get the HOA disclosure before signing, you have three days to void the contract.

 Location and the area
 9 questions 
 Beaches, drive times, schools, shopping and healthcare.
 How far is SeaFlower from the beach, really? The developer's site plan measures 3.2 miles to the beach. Cardel publishes drive times of 8 minutes to Bradenton Beach, 12 to Coquina Beach, 18 to Longboat Key and 24 to Anna Maria Bayfront Park; M/I lists Anna Maria Island at 7.2 road miles. The honest caveat: Cortez Road is the bridge road to the island, and in season (mid-February to mid-April, worst in March) beach traffic backs up. Go before 10 a.m. or after 1:30 p.m. and it is a short drive; try at noon on a March Saturday and it is not.

 How far to Sarasota, Tampa and the airports? Sarasota-Bradenton International (SRQ) is about 18 minutes and 8 miles. Tampa International is about 65 minutes and 37 miles; St. Pete-Clearwater about 55 minutes. Downtown Bradenton is about 6 miles, downtown Sarasota about 13 miles, UTC mall about 26 minutes and St. Armands Circle about 28 minutes, per builder-published drive times.

 What schools are SeaFlower homes zoned for? Sea Breeze Elementary and Bayshore High are listed by every builder. The middle school is disputed: Pulte and Cardel list W.D. Sugg Middle, while David Weekley lists Electa Lee Magnet Middle. Confirm the zone for a specific address with the Manatee County School District locator. Private options nearby include IMG Academy (adjacent), Bradenton Christian, Saint Stephen's Episcopal, St. Joseph Catholic and Cardinal Mooney, and Manatee offers school choice. Details on the location page .

 Is it near IMG Academy? Yes, IMG Academy's 600-acre campus is next door; the developer describes it as adjacent and Pulte lists it at three miles by road. That is a plus for anyone connected to IMG and a neutral for everyone else; campus traffic is on 34th Street West and El Conquistador, not inside the community.

 What hospitals and healthcare are close? HCA Florida Blake Hospital is about 8 minutes away; Manatee Memorial about 16 minutes; Sarasota Memorial roughly 25 minutes; Tampa General and Moffitt about 65 to 70 minutes. Urgent care and dental are planned in the Village Center (PacDental is a signed tenant).

 What is nearby for shopping, dining and things to do? Until the Village Center opens, the closest Publix and everyday retail are on Cortez Road and Manatee Avenue West. Nearby: the Cortez fishing village and Bridge Street (10 minutes), Robinson Preserve (14), Palma Sola Botanical Park, Manatee County Golf Course (5), IMG Golf Club (8), LECOM Park for Pirates spring training (15), and the Bradenton Riverwalk (16), per Cardel's drive times. Anna Maria Island's restaurants are the weekend default.

 What is the zip code and address? Bradenton, FL 34210, in unincorporated Manatee County. Streets include Flower Fields Trail, Seaflower Parkway, Reflection Parkway, Addison Avenue, Merritt Avenue, Fulham Avenue, Sunset Gardens Street and Lake Flores Avenue.

 How does SeaFlower compare to Lakewood Ranch? Lakewood Ranch is 33,000 acres, inland, with dozens of villages, two town centers and 1,064 new-home contracts in the first half of 2026. SeaFlower is 1,175 acres, three miles from the Gulf, with five builders on one plan and 198 contracts in the same period. Both have district assessments (Lakewood Ranch's Stewardship District, SeaFlower's Lake Flores CDD). Lakewood Ranch is finished infrastructure and a long commute to the beach; SeaFlower is the beach side and a community still being built. I have sold in both; which is right depends on whether you want it done now or want to be near the water.
 Insider perspective 
 What other new-construction options are there near the beach in Bradenton? Very few at SeaFlower's price point. Aqua by the Bay (Medallion) is lagoon-front and starts above $1 million; Eagle Trace (Neal) is maintenance-included with no CDD but a much higher HOA; Palma Sola Trace and Harbour Isle are largely built out. Most other new construction in Manatee County is east of I-75 in Lakewood Ranch or Parrish, 30 to 45 minutes from the sand.
 Insider perspective 

 Buying process and incentives
 10 questions 
 Agents, contracts, deposits, lenders and negotiation.
 Do I need my own agent to buy from a builder? Does it cost more? You do not need one, but the on-site sales consultant works for the builder, is paid by the builder and is measured on the builder's numbers. A buyer's agent on new construction is paid by the builder, so it does not raise your price. Under the 2024 rules you will sign a written buyer agreement that states what you owe (typically nothing if the builder pays), and compensation is negotiable. I represent buyers only.

 Do I have to bring my agent to the first visit? Most builders require it, or at least require the agent to register you before you walk in. If you tour unaccompanied and unregistered, some builders will refuse to pay your agent later, which means you lose representation for that builder. Call or text me before your first model visit and it is handled in five minutes.
 Insider perspective 
 How do builder incentives actually work? They are usually tied to the builder's affiliated lender: Pulte's rate offers run through Pulte Mortgage, M/I's advertised FHA rate through M/I Financial, David Weekley's through Grace Home Lending, Cardel's through a preferred lender. The builder pays for a rate buydown or closing-cost credit as an interested-party contribution, which lenders cap at 3%, 6% or 9% of price depending on your down payment. You are never required to use the affiliated lender, but the incentive usually disappears if you do not, so the comparison is total cost with the incentive versus an outside lender's rate.

 Can you negotiate price with a builder? Base price rarely moves on a to-be-built home; incentives, lot premiums, closing-cost credits, design-center credits and structural option pricing all can. Quick move-in homes are different: Pulte cut one listing by $10,000 and townhomes on Sunset Gardens Street were reduced $10,000 to $25,000 in 2026. Timing matters most. Builders push hardest in the last two weeks of a fiscal quarter, and division managers can approve what the on-site rep cannot.
 Insider perspective 
 Quick move-in or to-be-built: which is the better deal? Quick move-ins carry the biggest discounts and rate buydowns because finished inventory costs the builder money every month, and you know exactly what you are getting. To-be-built homes get you the lot, the plan and the finishes you want at base price plus options, six to fourteen months out, with more exposure to rate changes. If a quick move-in has the lot and 80% of the finishes you would have chosen, it is almost always the better deal.
 Insider perspective 
 Do I have to use the builder's lender? No. Pulte says so explicitly and it is true of all five. The catch is that rate and closing-cost incentives are conditioned on the affiliated lender. Get an outside quote anyway; sometimes the outside rate beats the bought-down rate once the fee structure is compared, and it always gives you leverage.

 What disclosures must I receive at contract? Two matter most. The HOA disclosure summary (Florida Statute 720.401) covering assessments and restrictions, with a three-day right to cancel if you did not get it before signing. And the bold-type CDD notice (Statute 190.048) stating that the Lake Flores Community Development District may levy taxes or assessments. You will also see the builder's warranty, the plan and elevation exhibits, and the option and deposit schedules.

 Can I pay cash or use a construction loan? Cash is accepted by every builder; Cardel publishes a draw schedule for cash buyers. Construction loans are less common with production builders, who finance the build themselves and close when the home is done; Cardel works with a preferred bank for construction lending on its semi-custom product.

 Can I tour without an appointment? Yes. The Welcome Center at 4505 Flower Fields Trail is open Monday to Saturday 9:30 to 5:30 and Sunday 12 to 6, and each builder's model is staffed daily: David Weekley at 7635 Addison Ave, Pulte at 7634 Addison Ave, Cardel at 4521 Flower Fields Trail, M/I at 8015 SeaFlower Parkway, and Issa through the Welcome Center. Register your agent first; text me before you go and I will set it up with every builder in five minutes.

 What does a good contract review catch? The default and deposit clauses, the completion window and what happens if the builder misses it, the escalation or cost-increase language, whether the appraisal gap is your problem, the change-order process, the warranty exclusions, and the arbitration clause. Builder contracts are written by the builder's lawyers and they are not the standard Florida resale contract. I read them with every client and refer out to a real estate attorney when something needs changing.
 Insider perspective 

 Out-of-state and relocation
 7 questions 
 Buying from a distance and becoming a Floridian.
 Can I buy and close remotely? Yes. Florida allows remote online notarization even when you are outside Florida, and the builders and their title companies handle mail-away and remote closings routinely. The developer offers live video appointments. Most of my clients see their home in person once or twice during the build and close from home.

 How do out-of-state buyers keep track of a build? Through their agent. I do video walkthroughs of the lot and the build at each stage, attend the pre-construction, pre-drywall and final meetings, and send the inspector's reports. Builders provide photos through their own portals, which are useful but selective.
 Insider perspective 
 Where are SeaFlower buyers coming from? The developer has not published data. From the sales floor: a lot of Manatee and Sarasota locals moving closer to the water, downsizers from Anna Maria Island and Longboat Key, and relocating buyers from the Northeast, the Midwest and Canada. The M/I townhomes and villas draw second-home and lock-and-leave buyers.
 Insider perspective 
 What do I need to establish Florida residency and homestead? A Florida driver license or ID card, Florida vehicle registration, and either voter registration or a declaration of domicile, plus Social Security numbers for all owners. Occupy the home by January 1 and file the homestead application with the Manatee County Property Appraiser by March 1.

 What are the utilities and who provides internet? Electric is Florida Power and Light, gas is TECO Peoples Gas, water and sewer are Manatee County, and internet is Bluestream fiber, which is included in the HOA fee at 1-Gig service.

 When is the best time of year to buy new construction here? Late in a builder's fiscal quarter and, especially, in September and December, when builders clear inventory before year-end reporting; that is when the largest buydowns and credits appear. Seasonally, summer is slower on the sales floor than February and March, when snowbird traffic peaks. Weather-wise, tour in July once and you will know whether Florida summers are for you.
 Insider perspective 
 Is west Bradenton a good place to live? It is older, established Florida: a working fishing village at Cortez, the causeway to Anna Maria Island, the Palma Sola Bay shoreline, IMG Academy, spring-training baseball at LECOM Park and a downtown Riverwalk. It is not the manicured, everything-new feel of Lakewood Ranch. SeaFlower is bringing new retail and homes to a part of the county that had very little new construction, which is a large part of why it is selling.
 Insider perspective 

 Investment, rentals and ADUs
 6 questions 
 What you can rent, and what it costs to hold.
 Can I rent out my SeaFlower home? Short-term? Whole-home leasing rules are in the HOA covenants, which are behind the resident portal; a third-party blog claims one year of owner occupancy before leasing, which I have not confirmed in an official document. For ADUs the rule is published: one year of owner occupancy first, then leases of six months or more. Assume no short-term rentals and verify the exact clause before you buy as an investment.

 What does it cost to hold a SeaFlower home as an investment? HOA of about $300 a month, the CDD assessment of roughly $1,475 to $4,605 a year by product and phase, property taxes at about 14.61 mills on full value with no homestead cap (non-homestead assessments are capped at 10% a year), and insurance. Lenders cap builder concessions on investment properties at 2% of price, so the incentive math is different from an owner-occupant's.

 Are the townhomes and villas good for a lock-and-leave second home? That is what they are designed for. M/I's 68 townhomes (3 bed, 2.5 bath, 2-car) and 90 twin villas (2 bed, 2 bath, 2-car) from $399,999 have exterior maintenance, insurance and reserves inside the HOA fee, so nothing needs your attention when you are away. Confirm what the HOA covers on roofs and exteriors in the villa documents.

 Can I rent the ADU and live in the main house? Yes, after one year of owner occupancy, with leases of six months or longer. That was the developer's stated design intent for the ADU program, and it is the most common way buyers here use one: a long-term tenant, a relative, or a home office that becomes a rental later.

 Is SeaFlower a good investment? Will values rise? Nobody can promise appreciation, and I will not. What the public record shows: strong absorption (about 270 homes sold in the first year), rising lot premiums, and MLS resales of new homes at roughly 99% of asking and $229 per square foot over the past year. What I watch: the Village Center opening, the Garden Club opening, and how the Phase 1C lots are priced relative to Phase 1B. Buy the house you want to live in at a number you can hold through a slow year; that is the only investment advice I give.
 Insider perspective 
 Can I do a 1031 exchange into a new-construction home here? Potentially, for an investment-use property, but the 45-day identification and 180-day closing windows are hard to meet on a to-be-built home. A quick move-in home is the realistic path. Talk to a qualified intermediary and your CPA before you sell the relinquished property.

 Hurricanes, flood zones and safety
 7 questions 
 The honest answers to the questions people are afraid to ask.
 Is SeaFlower in a flood zone? Do I need flood insurance? FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer shows the interior of the site as Zone X, minimal flood hazard, on FIRM panel 12081C0284F effective August 2021, with 0.2%-annual-chance and coastal AE and VE zones west of 86th Street toward Palma Sola Bay and isolated Zone A pockets near the 75th Street edge. Lenders do not require flood insurance in Zone X, but roughly one in three flood claims come from low- and moderate-risk zones and Zone X policies are inexpensive. Confirm your specific lot on Manatee County's flood map before you rely on any of this.

 What is the evacuation level, and how is that different from the flood zone? They are different systems. The FEMA zone is about rainfall and surge insurance risk; Manatee County's evacuation levels A through E are about storm surge and who leaves first. Look up a specific address on the county's Learn Your Level map before you buy. Elevation certificates for finished homes are available through the county records office.

 What happened here during Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024? SeaFlower was pre-construction; the first homes started in early 2025. Nearby, Anna Maria Island and the low-lying Cortez village took surge damage while Zone X neighborhoods two to four miles inland reported wind and debris but not water. Every home in SeaFlower is being built to the code that came after those storms.

 How wind-resistant are the homes, and does that lower insurance? They are built to the current Florida Building Code, which is updated every three years and cannot be weakened locally. Florida law requires insurers to give discounts for code compliance and wind-mitigation features such as roof-to-wall connections and opening protection, and new homes qualify through a wind-mitigation inspection form. That is the main reason new construction insures for less than older homes at the same address.

 Are the homes generator-ready? One of the developer's published buyer stories cites generator readiness as a reason for choosing a Cardel home, and natural gas service through TECO makes a standby generator practical. Whether a plan is pre-plumbed for one is a builder option; ask for it before the slab.

 Will Cortez Road traffic get worse with 4,000 homes? It is the most common objection online and it deserves a straight answer: yes, more homes mean more trips, and Cortez Road is the only bridge road to the island. The plan mitigates it with an internal trail network and a Village Center that keeps daily errands off the road, and the Cortez bridge replacement is a pending state project. I have not seen a published traffic study. If your daily commute is across that bridge, drive it at 8 a.m. in March before you buy.
 Insider perspective 
 Is the density too high? Are the homes close together? Lots run 42 to 60 feet wide for most single-family homes, which is closer than a 1990s subdivision and typical of coastal-village design; the trade is walkability, porches and a short walk to parks. Rear-load lots feel tighter in the back and more open on the street. If you want space between houses, the 60-foot and 80-foot lots exist; walk a finished street before you decide.

# SeaFlower HOA fees explained: what $300.88 a month actually covers, by home type

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/seaflower-hoa-fees-explained/
The official numbers, what is inside them, why the internet shows five different figures, and the one thing that will change after The Garden Club opens.

Home 
 Blog 
 Costs & fees

 Costs & fees

 SeaFlower HOA fees explained: what $300.88 a month actually covers, by home type

 The official numbers, what is inside them, why the internet shows five different figures, and the one thing that will change after The Garden Club opens.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 If you search "SeaFlower HOA fees" you will find $163, $277, $300, $380, $526 and $983. Only one set of those numbers comes from the association itself. Here it is, and here is why the others exist.

 The official figures

 The developer's HOA and CDD information sheet dated December 8, 2025, and David Weekley's community pages, both list the same monthly assessments:

 Home type Monthly HOA 
 Single-family home $300.88 
 Townhome (M/I Row Home) $308.43 
 Twin villa (M/I Village Home) $327.70 

 The association is SeaFlower Homeowners Association, Inc., managed by ICON Management. The fee is billed by the HOA, separately from the CDD assessment that appears on your tax bill.

 What is inside the number

 Every home's fee includes 1-Gig fiber internet from Bluestream, front and rear yard landscape maintenance, upkeep of the parks, trails and common areas, and operation of The Garden Club once it opens. Townhome and villa fees add exterior maintenance, insurance and reserves for the shared structures, which is why they are slightly higher and why they suit owners who are away part of the year.

 Two items are not inside it. The Lake Flores CDD assessment is separate and runs roughly $1,475 to $4,605 a year depending on phase and lot; it is on the tax bill. And the clubhouse portion of the HOA is currently abated. The sheet says it will be added at substantial completion of The Garden Club, scheduled for fall 2026. Expect the fee to step up then. How much is not published.

 Why the internet disagrees

 Listing portals compute HOA fees from MLS entries, which agents enter as monthly, quarterly or annual amounts and which the portals convert inconsistently. A $925 to $983 "townhome" figure is almost certainly a quarterly amount ($308.43 times three is $925.29). A $163 low end is a partial figure. A $380 villa figure came from an agent blog written before the information sheet was published. When a number does not match the HOA's own sheet, trust the sheet.

 How to compare it with other communities

 Add back what the fee includes. A community with a $150 HOA that leaves you paying $90 a month for internet and $150 for lawn care costs more than SeaFlower's $300.88. Lakewood Ranch villages vary widely and most sit inside a Stewardship District assessment on top of the HOA. The fair comparison is total recurring cost: HOA plus district assessment plus what you would buy separately.

 Trent’s take
 When I compare communities for a client I build one column: HOA, CDD or stewardship assessment, lawn, internet, and any amenity or gate fee. SeaFlower usually lands in the middle of the pack for a single-family home and near the top for what you get. The abated clubhouse portion is the number to ask about; I would budget for a meaningful increase after opening rather than be surprised.

 What to get in writing before contract

 Florida law requires the builder to give you an HOA disclosure summary before you sign, with a three-day right to cancel if it is missing. Ask for the current adopted budget, the declaration of covenants, the architectural guidelines, the amount of any capital contribution or working-capital fee at closing, and the projected assessment once the clubhouse portion is added. The last two are not published anywhere.

 Sources: SeaFlower HOA and CDD information sheet (Dec 8, 2025); David Weekley SeaFlower Classic and Bungalow pages (Sep 3, 2026); ICON Management resident portal; Florida Statute 720.401.

# Lake Flores CDD: the official per-lot assessment table and what it means for your tax bill

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/lake-flores-cdd-assessments-explained/
The district's own FY2027 numbers by phase and lot width, why Phase 1C costs more, and the answer to 'are CDD fees forever?'

Home 
 Blog 
 Costs & fees

 Costs & fees

 Lake Flores CDD: the official per-lot assessment table and what it means for your tax bill

 The district's own FY2027 numbers by phase and lot width, why Phase 1C costs more, and the answer to 'are CDD fees forever?'

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Out-of-state buyers meet the CDD on their first Florida new-construction purchase, usually on the first tax bill. Here is what the Lake Flores Community Development District is, what it costs on each SeaFlower lot, and how to read it.

 What a CDD is

 A Community Development District is a special-purpose local government created under Chapter 190 of the Florida Statutes. It sells tax-exempt bonds to pay for a community's infrastructure and repays them through an annual assessment on every lot, collected on the county tax bill. At SeaFlower the district is the Lake Flores CDD, created by Manatee County Ordinance 22-04 on January 11, 2022, covering about 1,181 acres and managed by Wrathell, Hunt and Associates. It paid for stormwater management, wetlands and conservation areas, the multi-modal trail, the alleys and the streetlights.

 The bonds behind the number

 Three bond series are outstanding: Series 2023A-1 ($23,375,000, maturing in 2054), Series 2023A-2 (largely prepaid by builders at lot closings in 2025 and 2026), and Series 2026 ($20,885,000, issued February 24, 2026 for Phase 1C). Your lot's annual debt assessment depends on which series financed it, plus an operations-and-maintenance charge of about $400 a year for everyone.

 The FY2027 proposed assessments

 Presented in May 2026 and heard in August 2026. Per lot, per year, including operations and maintenance:

 Phase Lot FY2027 proposed, per year 
 Phase N1 Townhome $1,473.49 
 Phase N1 Twin villa $1,580.99 
 Phase 1B1 42' $1,753.00 
 Phase 1B1 45' $1,849.75 
 Phase 1B1 50' $2,011.00 
 Phase 1B1 60' $2,333.50 
 Phase 1B1 80' $2,978.51 
 Phase 1B2 45' $2,091.63 
 Phase 1B2 50' $2,279.75 
 Phase 1B2 60' $2,656.01 
 Phase 1B2 80' $3,408.52 
 Phase 1C 42' $3,334.52 
 Phase 1C 45' $3,546.24 
 Phase 1C 50' $3,899.09 
 Phase 1C 60' $4,604.78 

 Two patterns matter. Phase 1B lots dropped in FY2027 because builders prepaid much of the 2023A-2 series at lot closing. Phase 1C lots are higher because the Series 2026 bonds are new and not prepaid; a 50-foot lot is $3,899 in Phase 1C versus $2,280 in Phase 1B2. David Weekley quotes $2,095.84 (Bungalow) and $2,660.36 (Classic) on its pages, which line up with the Phase 1B2 45- and 60-foot figures.

 Are CDD fees forever?

 The debt portion ends when the bonds mature, 2054 for the 2023 series and 2056 for the 2026 series, and it can be prepaid in a lump sum at any time, which many buyers do when they pay off a mortgage. The operations-and-maintenance portion continues indefinitely, because the district keeps maintaining the lakes, wetlands, trail and lights. So: the big part ends or can be ended; the small part is permanent.

 How it shows up

 As a non-ad valorem line on your Manatee County tax bill every November, with up to a 4% discount for early payment. Because it is a fixed amount tied to the lot, it does not rise with your home's value. Lenders include it in escrow, which is why the first November surprises people who budgeted from a builder's payment estimate.

 Trent’s take
 The single most useful question to ask a sales consultant is "which phase is this lot in?" It changes the CDD by more than $1,500 a year on identical lots and it tells you how finished the streets around you will be when you move in. The second most useful question is whether the builder will pay down any of the debt assessment as an incentive; a few production builders will on slower-moving lots, and it is worth more than a design credit because it compounds every year.

 The disclosure you will sign

 Florida Statute 190.048 requires a bold-type notice in the purchase contract that the Lake Flores Community Development District may levy taxes or assessments. Read it as a prompt to ask for the current assessment for your specific lot, in writing.

 Sources: Lake Flores CDD FY2027 proposed budget and FY2026 adopted budget (lakeflorescdd.net); district ordinance 22-04; developer HOA and CDD information sheet (Dec 8, 2025); David Weekley SeaFlower pages (Sep 3, 2026).

# David Weekley at SeaFlower: Bungalow vs Classic, from a former Weekley operations manager

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/david-weekley-bungalow-vs-classic-seaflower/
Twelve plans on two lot sizes, what each collection is really for, and what I checked on these homes when signing them off was my job.

Home 
 Blog 
 Builders

 Builders

 David Weekley at SeaFlower: Bungalow vs Classic, from a former Weekley operations manager

 Twelve plans on two lot sizes, what each collection is really for, and what I checked on these homes when signing them off was my job.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 I spent a year in operations with David Weekley Homes, doing the final quality-control walk before homes were handed to buyers, and for a stretch I oversaw SeaFlower itself. So this is the one builder page where I can tell you not just what they sell but how the homes go together.

 Two collections, two lot widths

 SeaFlower – Bungalow Homes · 45' · From the $500s
 Plan Base price Sq ft Beds Baths Garage 
 The Malone $469,990 1,615 2–3 2 2-car 
 The Bellmeade $485,990 1,791–1,839 3 2 2–3 car 
 The Ambrosia $507,990 1,958 3 2 2-car 
 The Marina $532,990 2,193 4 3 2-car 

 SeaFlower – Classic Homes · 60' · From the $600s
 Plan Base price Sq ft Beds Baths Garage 
 The Blairmore $624,990 2,343–3,172 4–5 2–3 + 1 half 2–3 car 
 The Cecelia $654,990 2,642–3,416 4–5 3–4 3-car 
 The Borrelli $664,990 2,506 4 3 2-car 
 The Wagoner $679,990 2,702–2,697 4 3 3-car 
 The Rubytail $689,990 2,850–2,992 4 3 + 1 half 2-car 
 The Bonham $694,990 2,882 4 3–4 + 0–1 half 3-car 
 The Del Ray $699,990 3,022–3,777 4–5 3–4 2–3 car 
 The Colston $709,990 3,030–3,026 4 3 4-car 

 Base prices as published on September 3, 2026, excluding lot premium and options. The Bungalow collection sits on 45-foot rear-load lots: garage in the alley, porch on the street, one- and two-story plans from 1,615 to 2,193 square feet. The Classic collection is on 60-foot lots, all one-story plans with optional bonus rooms that push square footage as high as 3,777, and a four-car garage on the Colston.

 Who each one fits

 Bungalow buyers want the village experience: a short walk to the trail and parks, a porch they will use, a garage they do not have to look at. The Marina is the only two-story plan, and it is the one for anyone who needs a fourth bedroom on a 45-foot lot. The Malone at 1,615 square feet is the most efficient plan in the community for a single-level home with a study.

 Classic buyers want a yard, a three-car garage, and single-level living with room to spare. The Borrelli's separate guest suite with its own bath is the plan people ask about when they need a second private suite; the Cecelia and Del Ray are the entertaining plans; the Colston is for the car collection.

 Models and quick move-ins

 The Bellmeade (Bungalow) opened July 8, 2025 at 7650 Seaflower Parkway and the Rubytail (Classic) opened August 27, 2025 at 7635 Addison Avenue, which is also the sales office. On September 3, 2026 Weekley listed three Bungalow quick move-ins on Reflection Parkway from $574,990 to $599,990 (ready October 2026 to January 2027) and one Classic Rubytail at 8202 Merritt Avenue for $882,990 (ready November 2026).

 Incentives, the honest version

 Weekley's September 2026 promotion, 7% off base price up to $40,000, explicitly excludes SeaFlower. That is the builder telling you this community sells without help. It does not mean nothing is negotiable; it means the conversation is about the lot premium, design-center credits and closing costs through Grace Home Lending, which Weekley owns 75% of and which you are not required to use. Compare its offer with an outside lender before you decide.

 What I checked on these homes, and still check

 Weekley's EnergySaver program is real: duct leakage tested before drywall, blower-door tested at completion, third-party inspection of insulation and air sealing, with a Tampa-average HERS score of 71. What I add for clients is an independent inspector at pre-drywall and at final, a review of the warranty document itself (one year workmanship, two years systems, ten years structural), and a walk of the alley and driveway with the buyer's actual vehicle on the rear-load lots.

 Trent’s take
 The Weekley trades at SeaFlower are the same crews that built the models, and the models are honest examples of the product. My advice is simple: pick the plan by how you live, pick the lot by which phase it is in and what backs up to it, and let me handle the lender comparison and the credits. Bring me in before your first visit so I can be registered.

 Sources: David Weekley SeaFlower Bungalow and Classic collection pages, plan pages and quick move-in listings (Sep 3, 2026); David Weekley promotion pages (Sep 3, 2026); David Weekley EnergySaver and warranty pages.

# Is SeaFlower in a flood zone? FEMA zone, evacuation level and what insurance really costs

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/is-seaflower-in-a-flood-zone/
What FEMA's map actually shows for the site, why the flood zone and the evacuation level are different questions, and the three documents to demand for your lot.

Home 
 Blog 
 Location

 Location

 Is SeaFlower in a flood zone? FEMA zone, evacuation level and what insurance really costs

 What FEMA's map actually shows for the site, why the flood zone and the evacuation level are different questions, and the three documents to demand for your lot.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 "Is SeaFlower in a flood zone?" is one of the most-searched questions about the community, and most of the answers online are a single word from a blog. Here is what the official sources say, and what they cannot say.

 What FEMA's map shows

 FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer, on flood insurance rate map panel 12081C0284F effective August 10, 2021, shows the interior of the SeaFlower site as Zone X, the designation for areas of minimal flood hazard. West of 86th Street, toward Palma Sola Bay, the map moves through the 0.2%-annual-chance zone into coastal AE and VE zones. Near the 75th Street West edge there are isolated Zone A returns, which usually mark ponds and wetlands rather than homesites. So the honest summary is: the homes are in Zone X, the community's western and eastern edges are not, and your lot is what matters.

 Three questions, three answers

 The FEMA zone determines whether a lender requires flood insurance. In Zone X it does not. The Manatee County evacuation level, A through E, determines who is told to leave ahead of a storm surge and is looked up by address on the county's Learn Your Level map; it is not the same as the flood zone and a Zone X home can sit in an evacuation level. The elevation certificate records the finished floor height of a specific home. Ask for all three for your lot. One agent video claims a 17-foot elevation for the community; I have not seen a document that supports a single number, and I would not repeat one until I had.

 Should you buy flood insurance anyway?

 Probably. FEMA's own data say roughly one in three flood claims come from low- and moderate-risk zones, and a Zone X policy through the NFIP or a private carrier is inexpensive. Manatee County participates in the Community Rating System, which discounts NFIP premiums 10% outside the special flood hazard area. Three miles from the Gulf, I recommend pricing one.

 Wind insurance is the bigger line

 Homeowner's insurance on the Gulf Coast is mostly about wind, and here new construction has a structural advantage. Every SeaFlower builder is building to the current Florida Building Code, which is updated every three years and cannot be weakened locally, and Florida law requires insurers to credit code compliance and mitigation features such as roof-to-wall connections and impact-rated openings. A wind-mitigation inspection form documents those credits. That is why a new home here insures for far less than a 1980s house at the same address. Get a real quote before contract and write an insurance contingency into your offer.

 What happened in 2024

 Hurricanes Helene and Milton hit before SeaFlower's first homes were built; construction started in early 2025. Nearby, Anna Maria Island and the low-lying Cortez village took surge damage, while Zone X neighborhoods two to four miles inland reported wind and debris but not water. Every home in SeaFlower is being built to the code that came after those storms, with impact glass or shutters, reinforced block first floors and underground utilities described in the developer's materials.

 Trent’s take
 Two things I do for every client here: I pull the FEMA zone and evacuation level for the specific lot, in writing, and I get an insurance quote from an independent agent before we sign. The builders' partners are fine, but a second quote has saved clients real money more than once. And yes, I buy the cheap Zone X flood policy on my own house.

 Sources: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (panel 12081C0284F); FloodSmart.gov; Manatee County floodplain management and evacuation level pages; Florida Statutes 553.73 and 627.0629; Pulse of Manatee (Nov 3, 2025) on construction timing.

# SeaFlower vs Lakewood Ranch: fees, commute, beach distance and what you are really choosing

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/seaflower-vs-lakewood-ranch/
I have sold in both. One is finished infrastructure an hour from the sand; the other is the beach side of the county with the amenity center still under construction.

Home 
 Blog 
 Comparisons

 Comparisons

 SeaFlower vs Lakewood Ranch: fees, commute, beach distance and what you are really choosing

 I have sold in both. One is finished infrastructure an hour from the sand; the other is the beach side of the county with the amenity center still under construction.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Rendering courtesy of the developer 

 I get this comparison on most strategy calls, and it usually comes down to one question I will get to at the end. First the facts.

 Scale and stage

 Lakewood Ranch is a 30,000-plus-acre master plan that has been building for three decades, with dozens of villages, two town centers, and 1,064 new-home contracts in the first half of 2026, the second-best-selling community in the country. SeaFlower is 1,175 acres, started sales in May 2025, and posted 198 contracts in the same period, which tied it for 51st nationally in its first full year. One is a finished city with new villages at the edges; the other is a first phase around a lake with the amenity center opening this fall.

 Beach distance

 This is the whole reason SeaFlower exists. The site plan measures 3.2 miles to the beach; builders quote 8 minutes to Bradenton Beach off-peak. From most of Lakewood Ranch the nearest Gulf beach is 30 to 45 minutes, longer in season, and that is the drive people underestimate when they buy for the weather and then never see the water.

 Fees

 Both carry district assessments on top of the HOA. Lakewood Ranch villages sit inside the Lakewood Ranch Stewardship District, with HOA fees that vary widely by village and by whether lawn care and gates are included. SeaFlower's HOA is $300.88 a month for a single-family home and includes fiber and full yard maintenance; the Lake Flores CDD runs roughly $1,475 to $4,605 a year by phase and lot. The fair comparison is total recurring cost, and it is village-specific; I run it for clients with the actual villages they are considering.

 Builders and product

 Lakewood Ranch has most of the national builders and price points from the $300s to several million. SeaFlower has five builders on one plan, from M/I townhomes at $399,999 to Issa estates above $1.25 million, with a coastal-village design code and an ADU allowance on every single-family lot that Lakewood Ranch villages do not offer.

 Amenities today versus amenities eventually

 Lakewood Ranch has decades of built amenities, parks, sports campuses and a hospital. SeaFlower's Garden Club and Village Center open in late 2026, and later-phase amenities are not yet on a plan. If you need everything working on move-in day, that is a real difference for the next year or two.

 Resale

 Lakewood Ranch has a deep, liquid resale market. SeaFlower's is just starting: the MLS shows about two dozen closings in the past year at roughly 99% of asking and $229 per square foot, mostly new-construction resales. Early buyers in first phases of well-executed master plans have generally done well over time; I will not promise that here, but the sales pace and rising lot premiums are the right early signs.

 Trent’s take
 The question I ask: do you want the beach to be part of your week, or a place you visit? If it is part of your week, SeaFlower is the only new-construction answer at this price on the beach side of Manatee County. If you want finished infrastructure, more restaurants tonight and a shorter drive to the interstate, Lakewood Ranch wins and I will happily show you the villages that fit. Plenty of my clients tour both in one day; I recommend it.

 Sources: RCLCO mid-year 2026 rankings via Sarasota Magazine (Jul 31, 2026); SeaFlower site plan and builder pages (Sep 3, 2026); Lake Flores CDD FY2027 budget; BEX Realty MLS summary (Sep 2026).

# Do you need a buyer's agent for new construction in Bradenton? What the sales counselor won't tell you

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/do-you-need-a-buyers-agent-for-new-construction/
The on-site consultant is good at the job, and the job is selling the builder's homes. What representation actually does, what it costs, and the registration rule that trips people up.

Home 
 Blog 
 Buying process

 Buying process

 Do you need a buyer's agent for new construction in Bradenton? What the sales counselor won't tell you

 The on-site consultant is good at the job, and the job is selling the builder's homes. What representation actually does, what it costs, and the registration rule that trips people up.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 I sat at the builder's sales desk for six years. I liked the buyers who came in with an agent and I liked the ones who did not, and I was measured the same way either way: on the builder's numbers. That is the whole answer, but here is the longer version.

 Who the sales consultant works for

 The builder. In Florida, licensees are presumed to be transaction brokers unless a different relationship is put in writing, and the on-site consultant is either the builder's employee or the builder's agent. They will be friendly, knowledgeable and genuinely helpful, and they will not tell you the lot premium is negotiable, which incentive the division manager can approve, or which paragraph of the contract you should push back on. It is not their job.

 What it costs you

 Nothing extra, in practice. Builders budget a co-broke commission on every sale and pay it to the buyer's agent at closing; they do not lower the price if you show up alone. Under the rules in place since August 2024 you will sign a written buyer agreement that states what you owe your agent, and compensation is negotiable; my agreements provide that the builder's payment satisfies it. The myth that you get a better deal without an agent is a line I heard on the sales floor, and it is not true.

 What representation does on a new build

 It reads the contract, which is the builder's document, not the standard Florida form: deposit and default clauses, completion windows, cost-escalation language, appraisal-gap terms, arbitration. It negotiates the things that move: lot premium, closing-cost credits, rate buydowns, design credits, structural option pricing, and timing. It compares the affiliated lender against an outside quote. It brings an independent inspector at pre-drywall and final, and attends the walkthroughs. And for out-of-state buyers it is the person on the ground every couple of weeks with a camera.

 The registration rule

 This is where buyers lose representation without knowing it. Most builders require your agent to accompany you or register you before your first visit to a model. If you tour on your own, some builders will not allow an agent to be added later, and you have just committed to buying that builder's home unrepresented. The fix takes five minutes: call or text me before your first visit and I register you with every builder in the community.

 Single agent or transaction broker?

 Ask any agent which relationship they are offering. Florida's default is transaction broker, a limited form of representation. A single agent owes fiduciary duties and must give you a written notice before showing property. I explain the difference on every first call so you can choose.

 Trent’s take
 I am not an on-site rep anymore, so I will say the quiet part: the best consultants in SeaFlower are very good, and a couple of them are friends of mine. Use them for what they know. Use me for what they cannot say. It costs you nothing and it changes the contract you sign.

 Sources: Florida Statute 475.278; NAR consumer guides on written buyer agreements and offers of compensation (2024); builder realtor pages (Sep 3, 2026).

# Quick move-in or to-be-built at SeaFlower: which is the better deal right now

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/quick-move-in-vs-to-be-built-seaflower/
Finished inventory carries the discounts and rate buydowns. To-be-built gets you the lot. How to decide, with the September 2026 numbers.

Home 
 Blog 
 Buying process

 Buying process

 Quick move-in or to-be-built at SeaFlower: which is the better deal right now

 Finished inventory carries the discounts and rate buydowns. To-be-built gets you the lot. How to decide, with the September 2026 numbers.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Every builder in SeaFlower sells both: homes already under construction with a price and a completion date, and lots you can pick a plan for. They are priced differently, negotiated differently and financed differently.

 Why quick move-ins are cheaper than they look

 A finished home costs the builder money every month it sits: construction loan interest, taxes, insurance, the sales team's attention. That is why inventory carries the incentives you see advertised. In September 2026, Pulte listed quick move-ins with "$10,000 in savings" (one Mabel II was cut from $675,405 to $665,405), M/I advertised a 4.875% FHA rate (5.644% APR) on select inventory, and M/I's townhome listings carried "was" prices. A quick move-in's price also already includes the lot premium and the options in the house, so it is closer to the real number than a base-price sign.

 What to-be-built gets you

 The lot you want, in the phase you want, with the structural options you want: the extra garage bay, the extended lanai, the ADU or garage suite, the pool bath. And finishes chosen by you rather than by the builder's design team for resale appeal. You pay base price plus lot plus options, you wait seven to fourteen months depending on the builder, and you carry rate risk during the build unless you lock with a forward commitment through the builder's lender.

 The math I run

 Take the quick move-in's price and subtract the value of its included options and lot premium to get an apples-to-apples base. Then add what you would actually spend on the to-be-built version: lot premium, the options you would choose, and the design-center budget (builders' own guidance runs 10% to 20% of base; most of my clients land at 5% to 15%). Compare the totals, then compare the monthly payments with each lender's incentive. A quick move-in with the right lot and 80% of the finishes you would have picked wins that comparison most of the time.

 When to-be-built wins

 When the lot matters: a lake, park or corner lot in a phase with a lower CDD assessment. When you need a structural feature no inventory home has, an ADU especially. When you are a year out anyway and can use the build time to sell a house elsewhere. And when the builder is releasing a new phase and pricing it to move.

 Timing

 Builders push hardest in the last two weeks of a fiscal quarter, and September and December are the months when inventory gets cleared before reporting. Homes that have passed their listed ready date without a contract are where the conversation about price and credits gets interesting.

 Trent’s take
 My honest bias: I steer most clients toward a quick move-in when one fits, because the incentive money is real and the home is inspectable before you close. I steer them to build when they want an ADU, a specific lot, or a plan the inventory does not cover. Either way I bring an inspector, and either way I run the lender math both ways before we sign.

 Sources: Pulte, M/I Homes and David Weekley SeaFlower quick move-in listings and promotions (Sep 3, 2026); Cardel Homes FAQ on build times and design-center spend; Fannie Mae selling guide on interested-party contributions.

# The honest pros and cons of buying in SeaFlower

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/honest-pros-and-cons-of-buying-in-seaflower/
Traffic, density, CDD debt, construction years and one pool for the first phase, weighed against the beach, the design and the sales pace.

Home 
 Blog 
 Community

 Community

 The honest pros and cons of buying in SeaFlower

 Traffic, density, CDD debt, construction years and one pool for the first phase, weighed against the beach, the design and the sales pace.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Rendering courtesy of the developer 

 I make a living helping people buy here, which is exactly why I owe you the case against it. Here are the objections I hear most, with what is true about each, and then the case for.

 The cons

 Cortez Road traffic. It is the only bridge road to Anna Maria Island, and in season, mid-February to mid-April, beach traffic backs up. Four thousand more homes will add trips. The plan mitigates it with the internal trail and a Village Center that keeps errands off the road, and the Cortez bridge replacement is a pending state project. There is no published traffic study I have found. If your daily routine crosses that bridge, drive it at the worst time before you buy.

 Density. Most single-family lots are 42 to 60 feet wide. That is closer than a 1990s subdivision and it is the price of walkability, porches and parks within a block. Rear-load lots feel tighter in the back and more open on the street. The 60- and 80-foot lots exist for people who want space.

 Paying for amenities before they open. HOA dues start at closing and the CDD lands on the first tax bill, while The Garden Club opens in fall 2026. The developer has abated the clubhouse portion of the HOA until then, which is the one concession, and the trail, parks and lawn service you are paying for exist now.

 One pool for Phase One. True: one amenity campus serves 1,063 homes. Later-phase amenities are not yet on a plan. Do not buy on the assumption of a second pool until it is.

 CDD debt. Roughly $1,475 to $4,605 a year by phase and lot, for decades, with bonds totaling tens of millions of dollars. It is disclosed, it is fixed, it can be prepaid, and it built the infrastructure you are enjoying. It is also money.

 Construction years. A community this size takes a decade or more. You will live near active construction, and the Village Center, apartments and hotel will build out around you. Some people find that energizing. Some do not.

 The pros

 The beach side of the county. 3.2 miles to the sand and almost no other new construction on this side of Manatee County. That scarcity is the whole thesis.

 The design. Four architectural styles, porches on the street, alleys, pocket parks, a golf-cart trail to a Publix, and an ADU allowed on every single-family lot. It is the most deliberate plan I have worked on.

 Five builders competing on one plan. M/I, Pulte, David Weekley, Cardel and Issa at prices from $399,999 to above $1.25 million, all competing for the same buyer, which keeps incentives honest.

 Sales pace and early recognition. About 270 homes sold in the first year and a national top-selling ranking from RCLCO in the first half of 2026. Builders do not release Phase 1C lots into a community that is not moving.

 New code, new systems. Impact openings, reinforced block first floors, underground utilities, current energy standards, and warranties from one to ten years. Insurance reflects it.

 Trent’s take
 My honest read: SeaFlower is a good buy for someone who wants the beach in their week, likes the village pattern of living, and can hold the home through the construction years at a payment that includes the CDD. It is a bad buy for someone who needs everything finished, wants a half-acre, or will resent the bridge traffic. I tell people which one they are on the first call, and I lose some of them to Lakewood Ranch. That is fine.

 Sources: SeaFlower developer pages and press releases (2025–2026); Lake Flores CDD budgets; RCLCO mid-year 2026 report; YouTube and Reddit comment threads reviewed Sep 3, 2026.

# SeaFlower construction timeline: Garden Club, Publix, Village Center, apartments, hotel and Phase Two

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/seaflower-construction-timeline/
A living page of what is built, what is under construction and what is promised, with dates as published. Updated as milestones land.

Home 
 Blog 
 Community

 Community

 SeaFlower construction timeline: Garden Club, Publix, Village Center, apartments, hotel and Phase Two

 A living page of what is built, what is under construction and what is promised, with dates as published. Updated as milestones land.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 3, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Rendering courtesy of the developer 

 Buyers in a first phase are buying a plan as much as a place, so here is the plan with dates as the developer, its partners and the press have published them. I update this page when a milestone changes.

 What is built

 The Welcome Center at 4505 Flower Fields Trail, a Cardel-built home with an 800-square-foot ADU, opened fall 2025.
 Models from all five builders; the last showcase homes (Issa and M/I) opened March 7, 2026.
 400 finished lots in Phases N1 and 1B, with the first residents moved in since September 2025.
 The 2.5-mile Lake Flores Trail sections around the first neighborhoods, lakes, pocket parks and streetlights (maintained by the CDD).

 Under construction

 The Garden Club: broke ground July 9, 2025; scheduled to open fall 2026.
 The Village Center: broke ground September 2025; retail, dining and office completion targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, with Publix and Publix Liquors slated for fall 2026. Dutch Bros has filed for its drive-thru on Cortez Road.
 Phase 1C: 384 lots under development through 2026, financed by the $20.9 million Series 2026 bonds issued February 24, 2026.
 Apartments: 332 to 362 units in the Village Center by NDC Development (sources differ on the count); delivery date not published.

 Promised, not yet dated

 The 120-room hotel in the Village Center; brand and start date unpublished.
 Phase Two, expected to begin around 2027 depending on market conditions, as the second of three roughly 400-acre phases.
 Amenities for later phases; none are on a published plan yet.
 Full buildout: about 4,000 homes, 600 apartments, 250 hotel rooms and 350,000 square feet of commercial space.

 The dated timeline

 2015 Manatee County approves the Lake Flores plan, including ADU zoning on every single-family lot. 
 Jan 2022 Lake Flores Community Development District created (Ordinance 22-04). 
 May 2024 Plans unveiled under the SeaFlower name; Publix announced as the first Village Center tenant in September 2024. 
 Jan 28, 2025 Preview Center opens at 8114 Cortez Road West. 
 Mar 2025 Builder plans and prices released; home sales begin in May 2025. 
 Jul 9, 2025 The Garden Club amenity center breaks ground. 
 Sep 2025 First residents move in; Village Center (CASTO and Redstone) breaks ground. 
 Late Oct 2025 Official grand opening; more than 138 homes sold by December. 
 Feb 24, 2026 CDD issues $20,885,000 Series 2026 bonds for Phase 1C. 
 Mar 7, 2026 Public model grand opening for new Issa Homes and M/I Homes showcase homes; 200+ homes sold in the first year. 
 Apr 10, 2026 784 of 1,063 Phase One homesites released; 384 more lots under development through 2026. 
 Jul 30, 2026 RCLCO ranks SeaFlower tied for 51st best-selling master-planned community in the U.S. with 198 contracts in the first half of 2026. 
 Fall 2026 The Garden Club and Publix scheduled to open; Village Center completion targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026. 
 About 2027 Phase Two expected to begin, timing dependent on market conditions. 

 Trent’s take
 What I watch, in order: the Garden Club opening, because it ends the abated HOA period and changes the fee; the Publix opening, because it changes daily life; and the pricing of Phase 1C lots relative to Phase 1B, because it tells you what the builders think demand looks like. I will update this page as each one lands.
