# SeaFlower rental rules: whole-home leasing, ADU leases, the apartments, and what the HOA documents govern

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/seaflower-rental-rules/
What is published, what is only claimed, what Florida law lets an HOA restrict, and how to verify before you buy as an investor.

Home 
 Blog 
 Investment

 Investment

 SeaFlower rental rules: whole-home leasing, ADU leases, the apartments, and what the HOA documents govern

 What is published, what is only claimed, what Florida law lets an HOA restrict, and how to verify before you buy as an investor.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Quick answer

 Two rules are published for SeaFlower: an accessory dwelling unit may be rented only after one year of owner occupancy in the main home, and ADU leases must be at least six months. Whole-home leasing rules live in the HOA covenants behind the resident portal; a third-party blog claims one year of owner occupancy before leasing, which is not confirmed in an official document on this site. Florida law lets an HOA prohibit rentals shorter than six months or more than three times a year and bind all owners, so assume short-term rentals are not permitted until the covenants say otherwise.

 What the law allows an HOA to do

 Florida Statute 720.306 lets an association amend its documents to restrict rentals of under six months or more than three times a year and apply that to every owner; other new rental restrictions bind only owners who buy after the amendment or consent to it. Unincorporated Manatee County cannot prohibit or limit the duration of vacation rentals under Statute 509.032 for rules adopted after 2011, so the HOA documents, not the county, are the operative rules here.

 The ADU program

 The developer's stated intent for the ADU allowance was long-term flexibility, not short-term rental: one year of owner occupancy first, six-month minimum leases after. A 2026 state bill proposed allowing local governments to permit shorter ADU rentals; check its status before planning around it.

 The apartments

 The Village Center includes 332 to 362 apartments in phase one (600 at buildout) by NDC Development. Rents and a leasing date have not been published; when they are, they will set the local benchmark for what a SeaFlower ADU or townhome can lease for.

 What an investor should verify before contract

 The current declaration of covenants and any leasing amendment, the ADU rule as written, the HOA's tenant-approval or registration process, and the capital contribution or transfer fee at closing. Get all of it in writing with the HOA disclosure summary Florida requires.

 Trent’s take
 I do not sell SeaFlower as a short-term-rental play, and I would be cautious of anyone who does. As a long-term rental or a home with an ADU that offsets the mortgage, it works, with the one-year owner-occupancy rule built into the plan.

 Sources: WUSF (Feb 5, 2026); Florida Statutes 720.306 and 509.032; seaflower.com Village Center posts; ICON Management resident portal (documents behind login).

# What SeaFlower's RCLCO ranking actually means: first-year sales in context

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/what-the-rclco-ranking-means-for-seaflower/
198 contracts in the first half of 2026, tied for 51st in the country and 17th in Florida, compared with Lakewood Ranch and Wellen Park, and why it matters to a buyer.

Home 
 Blog 
 Market update

 Market update

 What SeaFlower's RCLCO ranking actually means: first-year sales in context

 198 contracts in the first half of 2026, tied for 51st in the country and 17th in Florida, compared with Lakewood Ranch and Wellen Park, and why it matters to a buyer.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Quick answer

 RCLCO, the real estate consultancy that ranks the country's best-selling master-planned communities twice a year, counted 198 new-home contracts at SeaFlower in the first half of 2026. That tied the community for 51st nationally and 17th in Florida in its first full year of sales. For comparison, Lakewood Ranch posted 1,064 contracts (second nationally) and Wellen Park 727 in the same period. For a 400-acre first phase with one amenity center under construction, that pace is the strongest public signal a buyer has that the plan is working.

 The numbers behind it

 Sales opened in May 2025. The developer reported 60-plus sales by August 2025, 138-plus before the October grand opening, 200-plus by March 2026 and, per Bradenton Magazine, more than 270 by June 2026. 784 of 1,063 Phase One homesites had been released by April 2026, and the CDD issued $20.9 million in Series 2026 bonds in February to build Phase 1C.

 What it means for a buyer

 Absorption this strong does three things. It tells the builders they can hold price, which is why David Weekley excluded SeaFlower from its September 7% promotion. It funds and accelerates the amenities and the Village Center, which are on schedule for late 2026. And it moves the best lots out of each release quickly, which is where lot premiums come from.

 What it does not mean

 It is not an appreciation forecast. Early-phase resales here are new-construction resales at roughly 99% of asking and $229 per square foot over the past year on the MLS; that is a healthy but short record. Rankings measure demand, not your exit price.

 How SeaFlower compares by size

 Lakewood Ranch and Wellen Park are tens of thousands of acres with dozens of villages; SeaFlower's 1,175 acres and single first phase put it in a different weight class. Landing in the national top 60 against that field, in year one, is the story.

 Trent’s take
 When a community sells this fast in its first year, the negotiating room moves from base price to incentives, lot premiums and inventory homes. That is exactly what I see on the ground here, and it is why my advice in 2026 has been to shop the quick move-ins hard and to buy the lot you want when it is released, not to wait for a price cut that the sales pace does not support.

 Sources: RCLCO mid-year 2026 report via Sarasota Magazine (Jul 31, 2026); seaflower.com news posts (Aug 2025 to Aug 2026); Bradenton Magazine (Apr 1 and Jun 1, 2026); BEX Realty MLS summary (Sep 2026).

# The history of SeaFlower: from the Preston gladiolus farm to Lake Flores to a coastal village

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/history-of-seaflower-preston-farm-lake-flores/
Ninety years of flowers, a 2015 approval, three names, and the family and developers behind the largest new community on Bradenton's coastal mainland.

Home 
 Blog 
 Community

 Community

 The history of SeaFlower: from the Preston gladiolus farm to Lake Flores to a coastal village

 Ninety years of flowers, a 2015 approval, three names, and the family and developers behind the largest new community on Bradenton's coastal mainland.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Rendering courtesy of the developer 

 Quick answer

 The 1,175 acres at Cortez Road and 75th Street West were farmed by the Preston family's Manatee Fruit Company for nearly 90 years, much of it as one of the country's largest gladiolus farms. Manatee County approved a master plan for the land in 2015 under the name Lake Flores; the project was rebranded SeaFlower before its 2024 unveiling, with the lake named Lake Flores for Flavia Florez Preston. Lake Flores Land Company, led by Ed Hill, is developing it with investment partner LAMB Properties. Sales began in May 2025 and the first residents moved in that September.

 The farm

 For most of the twentieth century the land was in flowers, with gladiolus the signature crop, and the fields were a west Bradenton landmark. The community's street names (Flower Fields Trail, Sunset Gardens Street), the Garden Club name and the flower motif all come from that history.

 The plan

 The 2015 approval set up roughly 4,000 homes, 600 apartments, a hotel and about 350,000 square feet of commercial space in three phases of about 400 acres each, with an unusual county allowance for an accessory dwelling unit on every single-family lot. Early names for the project included Crossroads and Lake Flores.

 SeaFlower

 The SeaFlower brand, the coastal-village design code with four architectural styles, and the five-builder lineup were unveiled in 2024. A preview center opened on Cortez Road in January 2025, builders released plans and prices in March 2025, models opened through 2025, and the grand opening came in late October 2025. The Garden Club broke ground in July 2025 and the Village Center in September 2025, both opening in late 2026.

 The people

 Ed Hill is the principal of Lake Flores Land Company. The developer's community relations team and, from opening, an Art of Living Director run programming. The brand and site plan are held by an affiliate, Cortez75W Investors, LLC.

 Trent’s take
 Knowing the history helps on a tour: the flat, open, sandy ground was farmed, not filled, and the lake was designed as the center of the plan rather than left over from it. It also explains why the county said yes to ADUs a decade before they were fashionable; the plan was written for a village, not a subdivision.

 Sources: Sarasota Magazine (Jun 7, 2024); Bradenton Herald via Yahoo News (May 22, 2024); Business Observer (Oct 31, 2025); seaflower.com history and development-team pages; Pulse of Manatee (Nov 3, 2025).

# Hurricane preparedness for a new SeaFlower home: code, evacuation levels, generators and a plan

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/hurricane-preparedness-new-seaflower-home/
What the current Florida Building Code gives you, how to find your evacuation level, what a natural-gas generator setup looks like, and the checklist for a storm week.

Home 
 Blog 
 Location

 Location

 Hurricane preparedness for a new SeaFlower home: code, evacuation levels, generators and a plan

 What the current Florida Building Code gives you, how to find your evacuation level, what a natural-gas generator setup looks like, and the checklist for a storm week.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Photo courtesy of the builder 

 Quick answer

 A new SeaFlower home is built to the current Florida Building Code, updated every three years and, by law, not weakened locally on wind resistance, with impact-rated openings or shutters, reinforced block first floors and underground utilities described in the developer's materials. Your evacuation level (A through E) is set by Manatee County by address, independent of the FEMA flood zone, and is what determines whether you are told to leave; look it up on the county's Learn Your Level map. Natural gas service through TECO makes a standby generator practical, and a transfer switch is a before-the-slab option.

 What the code gives you

 Roof-to-wall connections, roof deck attachment and secondary water resistance, opening protection, and wind-load design for the coastal zone. A wind-mitigation inspection documents these for your insurer and they are the reason new construction here insures for less than older homes.

 Evacuation level versus flood zone

 FEMA's flood zone (Zone X for the interior of SeaFlower) is an insurance map. Manatee County's evacuation levels are a surge map used for orders. A Zone X home can sit in an evacuation level. Look up your specific address before you buy, and keep the county's alert app on your phone once you move.

 Generators and gas

 TECO Peoples Gas serves the community. A standby generator on natural gas removes the fuel-storage problem that portable generators have. Ask the builder for a transfer-switch pre-wire and a gas stub before the slab; one of the developer's published buyer stories cites generator readiness as a reason for choosing their home.

 The storm-week checklist

 Confirm shutters or impact glass on every opening; photograph the home for insurance; bring in patio furniture and cart; fill the car; fill prescriptions; know the evacuation route (Cortez Road east to I-75) and the county shelter list; keep the elevation certificate, wind-mitigation form and policy numbers in cloud storage.

 What happened in 2024

 Hurricanes Helene and Milton hit before SeaFlower's first homes were built. Nearby Anna Maria Island and low-lying Cortez took surge damage; Zone X neighborhoods a few miles inland reported wind and debris but not water. Every home here is being built to the code that followed.

 Trent’s take
 I tell every buyer the same three things: know your evacuation level, buy the cheap flood policy anyway, and pre-wire for a generator before the slab because it costs a fraction of retrofitting. New construction is the best hurricane answer on this coast; it is not a reason to skip the plan.

 Sources: Florida Statute 553.73; Manatee County Emergency Management evacuation levels; FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer; seaflower.com buyer stories (Jun 1, 2026); David Weekley utility listings (TECO Peoples Gas).

# Rear-load vs front-load lots at SeaFlower: yards, pools, alleys and daily life

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/rear-load-vs-front-load-lots-seaflower/
Which builders offer which, what an alley garage changes about your lot, and the questions to ask before you choose.

Home 
 Blog 
 Community

 Community

 Rear-load vs front-load lots at SeaFlower: yards, pools, alleys and daily life

 Which builders offer which, what an alley garage changes about your lot, and the questions to ask before you choose.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Photo courtesy of the builder 

 Quick answer

 Rear-load (alley) lots put the garage behind the home, so the street side is porch and windows and your driveway is a short apron off the alley. Front-load lots face the garage to the street and usually come with a deeper back yard. David Weekley's Bungalow homes on 45-foot lots are rear-load; Cardel offers front- and rear-garage versions of most of its 50- and 60-foot plans; Pulte offers both; M/I's townhomes have rear-load detached garages. The choice decides your yard depth, pool feasibility, guest parking and how the street looks.

 What rear-load changes

 The street face is the best-looking side of the house, which is the whole point of the village design. Guest parking is on the street in front. The back yard is smaller because the garage and its apron take the rear of the lot; a pool is possible on some plans and not others. Alleys are narrow; measure a long truck or a trailer against the turning radius before you commit, and note where the trash pickup happens.

 What front-load changes

 A conventional driveway, a deeper back yard, easier pool and lanai extensions, and a street view that includes the garage door. Cardel's and Pulte's front-load versions exist precisely because some buyers want the yard more than the porch.

 Carts, trailers and boats

 Rear-load lots are where most residents will park a golf cart, right off the trail network. Boats and large trailers are the wrong fit for the village lots; ask the HOA about vehicle rules before you buy either.

 Resale

 Neither is better; they attract different buyers. The porch-forward rear-load streets are what the community markets and what photographs well; the front-load lots serve people who need the yard.

 Trent’s take
 Walk a finished rear-load street and a front-load street on the same visit, then stand in the alley with your car keys in your hand. The decision is usually obvious in ten minutes, and it should be made before you pick a builder, because it narrows the field.

 Sources: David Weekley Bungalow collection page; Cardel Homes plan pages (front and rear garage versions); Pulte SeaFlower page; M/I Homes SeaFlower page (Sep 3, 2026).

# Natural gas at SeaFlower: what it means for cooking, hot water, generators and your builder choice

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/natural-gas-at-seaflower/
TECO Peoples Gas serves the community. Which builders make it standard, what to stub before the slab, and the cost logic.

Home 
 Blog 
 Community

 Community

 Natural gas at SeaFlower: what it means for cooking, hot water, generators and your builder choice

 TECO Peoples Gas serves the community. Which builders make it standard, what to stub before the slab, and the cost logic.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Quick answer

 SeaFlower has natural gas service through TECO Peoples Gas; David Weekley lists TECO as the community's gas utility and Cardel markets itself as a natural-gas builder here. Which appliances run on gas varies by builder and plan, so ask for the specification sheet: a gas range, tankless water heater, dryer connection, outdoor grill stub and a standby generator are the usual candidates, and every one of them is far cheaper to plumb before the slab than after.

 Why it matters on the Gulf Coast

 Most new communities in the region are all-electric. Gas gives you a range that cooks like one, a tankless water heater that never runs out, and a generator that does not need fuel cans. In a hurricane week, the generator is the reason people ask.

 What to specify before the slab

 Gas stubs are under the slab or in the walls: range, water heater, dryer, outdoor kitchen or grill, fire pit, pool heater, and the generator connection with a transfer switch. Add the ones you might want; the stub is inexpensive at framing and expensive later.

 Builder by builder

 Cardel: natural-gas community, gas appliances featured in models. David Weekley: TECO listed as the gas utility; which appliances are standard versus optional is on the included-features sheet, which is not published, so ask. Pulte, M/I and Issa: confirm on site; gas availability at the lot does not guarantee gas appliances in the base specification.

 Cost

 A gas account adds a monthly service charge and usage; in exchange, water heating and cooking loads come off the electric bill. The generator is the large ticket: a standby unit with automatic transfer is a five-figure item; the pre-wire and stub during construction are not.

 Trent’s take
 If you are choosing between two builders and one gives you a gas range and tankless heater as standard, that is worth real money in the comparison. And if a generator is on your list at all, get the stub and the transfer switch in the contract now.

 Sources: David Weekley SeaFlower community pages (utility listings); Cardel Homes SeaFlower page (Sep 3, 2026); TECO Peoples Gas service information.

# Builder warranties at SeaFlower explained: 1-2-10, what is covered, and how to use yours

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/builder-warranties-explained-1-2-10/
What each builder publishes, what the years actually mean, what is excluded, whether it transfers, and the eleven-month walk that protects you.

Home 
 Blog 
 Buying process

 Buying process

 Builder warranties at SeaFlower explained: 1-2-10, what is covered, and how to use yours

 What each builder publishes, what the years actually mean, what is excluded, whether it transfers, and the eleven-month walk that protects you.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Quick answer

 David Weekley publishes a 1-2-10 warranty (one year workmanship and materials, two years mechanical systems, ten years major structural). Pulte publishes a 10-year limited structural warranty that transfers to later owners. M/I publishes a 10-year transferable structural warranty plus one-year customer care coverage. Issa publishes one year on materials and workmanship, two years on roofing, plumbing, electrical and HVAC, and ten years structural through RWC. Cardel's terms are not on its public pages. The warranty document, not the brochure, defines coverage; read the exclusions and the claim process before closing.

 What the years mean

 Year one covers workmanship and materials: drywall, trim, paint, doors, tile, caulk, cosmetic items reported in the window. Years one to two cover the systems: plumbing, electrical, HVAC. Years one to ten cover major structural defects, usually defined narrowly (foundation, load-bearing walls, columns, beams) and often administered by a third-party warranty company. Appliances carry the manufacturers' warranties.

 What is usually excluded

 Normal settling and shrinkage cracks below a stated size, damage from lack of maintenance, landscaping, weather events, items you altered, and anything cosmetic reported after the first-year window. Transferability to a later owner varies; Pulte and M/I say theirs transfer.

 How to use it

 Report in writing through the builder's warranty portal or email, with photos and dates. Batch cosmetic items into a list before the one-year deadline rather than one at a time. Keep every closing document: warranty booklet, wind-mitigation form, elevation certificate, selection sheets.

 The eleven-month walk

 Hire an independent inspector at eleven months to catch drywall cracks, nail pops, settling, grading and drainage, and system issues before the workmanship warranty expires. The list you submit at month eleven is the most valuable warranty claim you will make.

 Trent’s take
 On the builder side I handled warranty calls, and the buyers who got the most out of the program were the ones who documented at final walkthrough and again at eleven months. Nobody was ever penalized for a thorough list submitted on time.

 Sources: David Weekley multi-level warranty page; Pulte 10-year warranty page; M/I Homes warranty statement; Issa Homes warranty page (Sep 3, 2026).

# Can you negotiate with a builder in SeaFlower? What moved in 2026 and what did not

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/can-you-negotiate-with-a-builder-in-seaflower/
Public evidence of price cuts and credits, the numbers that never move, and the order and timing that get results.

Home 
 Blog 
 Buying process

 Buying process

 Can you negotiate with a builder in SeaFlower? What moved in 2026 and what did not

 Public evidence of price cuts and credits, the numbers that never move, and the order and timing that get results.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Quick answer

 Yes, within limits. In 2026 the public record shows Pulte cutting a quick move-in from $675,405 to $665,405 and flagging "$10,000 in savings" on others, M/I showing "was" prices across its inventory and advertising a bought-down FHA rate, Cardel offering up to $20,000 in design options, and MLS townhome listings reduced by $10,000 to $25,000. What did not move: base prices on to-be-built homes, and David Weekley, which excluded SeaFlower from its September 7% promotion. The negotiable levers are lot premium, closing-cost credit, rate buydown depth, design and option credits, and inventory pricing, in roughly that order.

 Why base price rarely moves

 A base-price cut resets the community's price sheet, angers buyers who paid more last month, and shows up in the builder's reporting. Credits and premium reductions do none of that, which is why builders prefer to give value through them. On a to-be-built home, treat base price as fixed and negotiate everything around it.

 Where the money is

 Lot premium on slower lots; closing-cost credits through the affiliated lender, often expandable at quarter-end; permanent rate buydowns, which cost the builder points and are worth more to you than an equivalent price cut; design-center and structural-option credits; and on inventory homes past their ready date, the price itself.

 Timing

 The last two weeks of March, June, September and December. September and December are strongest because builders clear inventory before year-end. Division managers can approve what on-site consultants cannot ask for, and that request goes through your agent.

 What a strong community changes

 SeaFlower sold fast in its first year, which is why base prices held and why Weekley did not need a promotion here. That does not remove negotiation; it moves it to inventory homes, incentives and premiums.

 Trent’s take
 The buyers who did best in SeaFlower this year did three things: they shopped inventory in the last two weeks of a quarter, they asked for the credit and the premium reduction together rather than a price cut, and they had an outside lender quote in hand when the rate buydown was offered. That is the playbook.

 Sources: Pulte, M/I Homes, Cardel and David Weekley SeaFlower pages and promotions (Sep 3, 2026); BEX Realty MLS listing history (Sep 2026); Fannie Mae interested-party contribution limits.

# How builder sales really works: what the on-site consultant can and cannot do for you

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/how-builder-sales-really-works/
Quotas, registration, the approval chain, the lender tie-in and quarter-end, from someone who sat at that desk for six years.

Home 
 Blog 
 Buying process

 Buying process

 How builder sales really works: what the on-site consultant can and cannot do for you

 Quotas, registration, the approval chain, the lender tie-in and quarter-end, from someone who sat at that desk for six years.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Quick answer

 The on-site sales consultant is a licensed, well-trained professional whose job is to sell the builder's homes at the builder's numbers. They can explain plans, lots, pricing and published incentives, and write the contract. They cannot approve a lot-premium reduction, an expanded credit or a base-price change; those go to a sales manager or division leadership, and the request usually has to come through your agent. They also cannot register your agent after you have toured unaccompanied at most builders.

 The job

 Consultants carry a monthly and quarterly quota, are measured on contracts written and closed, and are coached on a process: greet, qualify, demonstrate, close. Good ones are genuinely helpful; I was one, and I liked the job. None of that changes who pays them.

 The approval chain

 Published incentives are pre-approved. Anything beyond them (premium reductions, larger closing-cost credits, deeper buydowns, design credits, CDD paydowns) requires a manager's approval and is easier to get at quarter-end when the division is chasing a number. The consultant is more likely to carry your request upstairs if it comes from an agent who will bring them the next buyer too.

 Registration

 Most builders pay a buyer's agent only if the agent accompanied you or registered you before your first visit. If you walk in alone and sign the guest card without an agent, some builders will not add one later. This is the single most common way buyers lose representation.

 The lender tie-in

 Rate offers and closing-cost credits are conditioned on the affiliated lender. The consultant will steer you there because the incentive structure depends on it. You are never required to use that lender; compare net cost.

 What to do with all this

 Use the consultant for what they know: plans, lots, availability, timelines. Use your agent for what they cannot say: what is negotiable, when, and how the contract should read. Both can be true at the same desk.

 Trent’s take
 Two of the best consultants in SeaFlower are people I would happily send my family to. I still register my clients before they walk in, because the day the deal gets hard is the day you want someone at the table who is paid by the buyer's side of the closing statement.

 Sources: builder realtor-registration pages and contact forms (Sep 3, 2026); NAR consumer guides on buyer agreements (2024); first-hand experience as a builder sales consultant and operations manager.

# Manatee County growth and what it means for SeaFlower: population, infrastructure and the west side

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/blog/manatee-county-growth-and-seaflower/
The county grew 23% in a decade and 10% more since 2020, nearly all of it east of I-75. SeaFlower is the exception, and that is the point.

Home 
 Blog 
 Market update

 Market update

 Manatee County growth and what it means for SeaFlower: population, infrastructure and the west side

 The county grew 23% in a decade and 10% more since 2020, nearly all of it east of I-75. SeaFlower is the exception, and that is the point.

 By Trenton Miller, MBA September 4, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 

 Independent buyer’s guide, not the developer’s or any builder’s site. Figures are as published on the dates noted and must be verified with the builder. Developer’s official site .

 Rendering courtesy of the developer 

 Quick answer

 Manatee County's population grew about 23% from 2010 to 2020 and roughly 10% more from 2020 to 2023, per figures the developer cites, and the region's growth has been concentrated east of I-75 in Lakewood Ranch and Parrish. West Bradenton, the coastal mainland, has had almost no new construction because there was almost no land. SeaFlower's 1,175 acres are the largest developable parcel on that side of the county, which is the scarcity argument behind the community and behind its first-year sales pace.

 Where the growth went

 Lakewood Ranch (1,064 new-home contracts in the first half of 2026) and Parrish's new communities absorbed most of the county's new households for a decade. The trade-off for those buyers is distance to the Gulf: 30 to 45 minutes to the nearest beach.

 What SeaFlower adds on the west side

 About 4,000 homes at buildout, 600 apartments, a hotel and 350,000 square feet of commercial space, three miles from Anna Maria Island, on the only large tract left. Phase One's 1,063 homes and the Village Center are the first new retail and housing at scale in west Bradenton in a generation.

 Infrastructure to watch

 The Cortez Road bridge replacement to Anna Maria Island (a pending state project), improvements on Cortez Road and 75th Street West, and how the county accepts and designates SeaFlower's internal streets. Traffic on the bridge road is the most common objection to the community online; the internal trail network and the Village Center are the plan's answer, and the bridge project is the state's.

 Schools and services

 The west side's public schools have modest third-party ratings, and the county has been adding capacity east. Blake Hospital, IMG Academy and downtown Bradenton are established anchors nearby.

 Trent’s take
 My honest read on growth: the east side of the county is where the volume is, and the west side is where the scarcity is. Buyers who want a new home and the beach in the same week have exactly one large-scale option, and that is why I spend so much of my time here.

 Sources: seaflower.com growth post citing county population figures (Jan 28, 2026); RCLCO mid-year 2026 via Sarasota Magazine; Business Observer (Oct 31, 2025); Reddit and YouTube public comments on Cortez Road traffic (2025–2026).

# About Trenton Miller: Former Builder Insider, SeaFlower Buyer's Agent

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/about/
Trenton Miller spent seven years on the builder side, six in sales with Pulte and Del Webb and one in operations with David Weekley Homes, where he briefly oversaw SeaFlower. Now he represents buyers only.

Home 
 About Trenton

 About Trenton Miller, MBA

 I sold homes for the builder. Now I make sure the builder treats you right. 

 Former Pulte top producer and David Weekley operations manager who briefly oversaw SeaFlower. Now an independent buyer’s agent for new construction on Florida’s Gulf Coast.

 Book a free strategy call Text 716-949-5557 

 7
 years on the builder side
 Pulte, Del Webb and David Weekley

 $150M + 
 in new-home sales
 as a builder top producer

 300 + 
 clients helped
 most relocating from out of state

 #1
 Salesperson of the Year
 Tampa Bay Builders Association

 Seven years on the builder side

 I grew up in Buffalo, New York, which explains the phone number and the enthusiasm for January in Florida. I spent seven years working for the biggest names in new construction on the Gulf Coast: six in sales and one in operations.

 On the sales side I was a top producer with Pulte and Del Webb, closing more than $150 million in new-home sales and earning the Tampa Bay Builders Association Salesperson of the Year award. I sat at the sales-center desk you sit across from. I wrote the contracts, ran the incentives, priced the lots, and watched what happened to buyers who walked in without anyone in their corner.

 Then I moved to operations as an Operations Manager with David Weekley Homes. One of my jobs was the final quality-control walk on every home before it was handed to a buyer. For a stretch, I oversaw the SeaFlower community itself for David Weekley: the lots, the models, the trades, the handoffs. I know what a good SeaFlower build looks like because signing off on them was my job.

 Why I switched sides

 The on-site sales consultant is paid by the builder, works for the builder, and is measured on the builder's numbers. That is not a criticism. It is just the job, and I did it well. But it means the person explaining the contract to you is not the person negotiating for you.

 I left to become that person. Found Your Florida is my buyer-representation practice, built entirely on new construction. I only represent buyers. I never list homes for builders. The builder still pays my commission, exactly as they budget for on every sale, so representation does not raise your price by a dollar.

 How I work with SeaFlower buyers

 Before you tour. Builders track who brought you. If you walk into a model unrepresented, some builders will not let an agent join later. A five-minute call before your first visit protects your options.
 Choosing a builder and lot. I walk SeaFlower every few weeks. I know which builder fits which budget and lifestyle, which lots carry premiums that hold value, and what is planned behind that "preserve" view.
 Negotiating. Incentives are a starting point, not a menu. I know what each builder's division can move on and when (fiscal quarter-ends matter more than anyone admits).
 During the build. I attend pre-construction, pre-drywall and final walkthroughs, and I bring an independent inspector. Problems get fixed while the builder still has to fix them.
 Out of state? Most of my clients are. I do video walkthroughs of the lot and the build, and I coordinate remote closings.

 What I am not

 I am not affiliated with SeaFlower, its developer, or any builder in the community. Nobody pays me to recommend them. If SeaFlower is not the right fit for you, I will tell you, and I will point you to a community that is. I am a licensed Florida sales associate with LPT Realty, LLC, and I hold an MBA. Real estate is a licensed profession; the details are in the footer.

 Why buyers bring me in
 Builder-paid representation costs you nothing extra. What you get is someone who has sat on the other side of the table.

 On the deal

 Seven years inside Pulte and David Weekley, over $150M in new-home sales.

 I know what builders will move on (closing costs, rate buydowns, lot premiums, design-center credits) and what they won’t.

 I read the fine print: escalation clauses, deposit terms, completion windows, appraisal gaps.

 On the build

 As Operations Manager at David Weekley, I did final quality-control walks before homes were delivered.

 I know what to flag at framing, pre-drywall and final walkthrough, and I bring an independent inspector.

 Most buyers find problems after closing. Mine find them while the builder still has to fix them.

# Accessibility

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/accessibility/
Accessibility statement for buyinginseaflower.com and how to request information in another format.

Home 
 Accessibility
 Accessibility

 Buying in SeaFlower is committed to making this site usable by everyone, including people who use assistive technology. We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA and test the site on an ongoing basis. Videos are captioned on YouTube, images include text descriptions, and all forms and menus can be operated by keyboard. If you have difficulty using any part of this site or need information in an alternative format, email trenton@foundyourflorida.com or call 716-949-5557 and we will provide it promptly.

 What we have done

 Semantic headings, landmarks and a skip link on every page.
 Keyboard-operable menus, accordions, filters, sortable tables and video players, with visible focus states.
 Text alternatives for images and a schematic map with a written description.
 Color contrast checked against WCAG 2.1 AA for body text and buttons.
 Videos are hosted on YouTube with captions available through the player.
 No pop-ups that block the page, and no third-party overlay widgets.

 Tell us

 If something does not work with your screen reader, magnifier or keyboard, email trenton@foundyourflorida.com or call 716-949-5557. We will fix it and, in the meantime, get you the information another way.

# Privacy Policy

URL: https://buyinginseaflower.com/privacy/
How buyinginseaflower.com collects and uses information, including text-message consent and your choices.

Home 
 Privacy
 Privacy Policy

 Effective September 3, 2026. This policy covers buyinginseaflower.com, published by Trenton Miller, Found Your Florida (LPT Realty, LLC).

 What we collect

 Information you send us. When you submit a form, book a call, or text or email me, I receive what you provide: typically your name, email, phone number, timeline and message. Forms note the page you were on and, if present, the marketing campaign that brought you (UTM parameters).
 Analytics. The site uses Google Analytics 4 with IP anonymization to understand which pages help people. It sets cookies and records device, browser, approximate location and pages viewed. Google's use of this data is described in its privacy policy.
 Embedded services. Videos are embedded from YouTube in privacy-enhanced mode (youtube-nocookie.com), which does not set tracking cookies until you press play. The booking page loads Calendly, which has its own privacy policy. If you book, Calendly collects the details you enter.

 How we use it

 To answer your questions and follow up about your home search, including by phone, text and email.
 To keep notes about your search in a customer-relationship system so I do not ask you the same questions twice.
 To send occasional market updates if you opt in. Every email has an unsubscribe link, and you can reply STOP to any text message.
 To improve the site.

 I do not sell your personal information. I share it only with services needed to run this site and my practice (for example, email, scheduling, CRM and analytics providers) and with my brokerage as required for real estate transactions.

 Text messages

 By providing a phone number and ticking the consent box, you agree to receive calls and texts from Trenton Miller / Found Your Florida (LPT Realty, LLC) about your home search, which may be sent using automated technology. Consent is not a condition of purchase. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out or HELP for help. Mobile information will not be shared with third parties for marketing purposes.

 Cookies and your choices

 You can block cookies in your browser and the site will still work. You can request a copy of the information I hold about you, ask me to correct it, or ask me to delete it by emailing trenton@foundyourflorida.com .

 Children

 This site is not directed to children under 13 and I do not knowingly collect their information.

 Changes

 If this policy changes, the effective date at the top will change with it. Questions: trenton@foundyourflorida.com or 716-949-5557.

 Terms
 Terms of Use

 Effective September 3, 2026.

 Informational only

 buyinginseaflower.com is an independent resource for people considering a home in SeaFlower, Bradenton, Florida. Content reflects public information from developers, builders and government sources, plus the professional opinions of Trenton Miller. It is not legal, tax, lending or engineering advice. Confirm every figure with the builder, developer, county or your own advisors before relying on it.

 Not affiliated

 Independent site. Information on this website is provided by Trenton Miller of Found Your Florida, a licensed Florida real estate sales associate with LPT Realty, LLC. This is not the official website of the SeaFlower® community. We are not associated with or affiliated with the SeaFlower® community or its developer, and the developer has not prepared or approved this website. The developer's official website is www.SeaFlower.com. We are likewise not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by Cortez75W Investors, LLC, Lake Flores Land Company, LAMB Properties, or any builder in the community, including David Weekley Homes, M/I Homes, Pulte Homes, Cardel Homes and Issa Homes. Trenton Miller was previously employed by David Weekley Homes and PulteGroup and is no longer associated with either company. All trademarks and service marks related to the SeaFlower® community are owned by the developer and its affiliates; builder and product names are trademarks of their respective owners and are used here only to identify the community and its builders.

 Accuracy

 Information disclaimer. Prices, floor plans, square footages, lot sizes, availability, incentives, HOA and CDD assessments, taxes, amenities, school assignments and completion dates are provided by builders, the developer and public sources. They are believed reliable but are not guaranteed, change without notice, may contain errors, and must be verified directly with the builder, developer or county before you rely on them. Prices shown are base prices as of the date noted on each page and exclude lot premiums, options, upgrades, closing costs and fees. Nothing on this site is an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy real property; offers can be made only through a builder's or seller's written purchase agreement. Buyer representation is by written agreement; broker compensation is not set by law and is fully negotiable.

 No agency relationship by browsing

 Reading this site, submitting a form or having a call does not create a client relationship. Buyer representation begins only when we sign a written agreement. Until then, no duty of representation is owed.

 Brokerage

 Fair Housing

 Equal Housing Opportunity. Trenton Miller and LPT Realty, LLC are pledged to the letter and spirit of U.S. policy for the achievement of equal housing opportunity throughout the Nation. We encourage and support an affirmative advertising and marketing program in which there are no barriers to obtaining housing because of race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status, or national origin. Every home and community described on this site is available to all persons on an equal-opportunity basis. Descriptions of communities and homes are about the property, not about who should live there.
